question:
The smallest blood vessel is called:

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: capillary
artery
vein
vena cava
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is capillary

Explanation:
Blood vessels are of three types: arteries, veins, and capillaries. Capillaries are the smallest blood vessels with a diameter of about 5-10 micrometers. They connect arteries and veins, facilitating the exchange of oxygen, nutrients, carbon dioxide, and waste products between blood and tissues. Their walls are extremely thin (single endothelial cell layer), allowing efficient diffusion. This is why capillaries are also called 'exchange vessels'.

Extra Facts:
1. The total length of capillaries in the human body is approximately 40,000 km, equal to Earth's circumference.
2. Capillaries consist of a single layer of endothelial cells, enabling material exchange.
3. Arteries carry oxygenated blood away from the heart, while veins return deoxygenated blood to the heart.

question:
In human beings which of the following has a high affinity for oxygen?

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: Hemoglobin
Carbon dioxide
White blood cells
Melanin
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Hemoglobin

Explanation:
Hemoglobin is a protein found in red blood cells (RBCs) that has a high affinity for oxygen. It contains an iron (Fe²⁺)-containing heme group, which binds oxygen reversibly to form oxyhemoglobin. This property allows hemoglobin to efficiently transport oxygen from the lungs to body tissues. The binding of oxygen to hemoglobin is cooperative, meaning the binding of one oxygen molecule increases the affinity for the next.

Extra Facts:
Hemoglobin's oxygen affinity is influenced by pH, temperature, and CO₂ concentration. The Bohr Effect states that high CO₂ levels and low pH (acidic environment) reduce hemoglobin's oxygen affinity, facilitating oxygen release in tissues. Hemoglobin deficiency leads to anemia. Fetal hemoglobin (HbF) has a higher oxygen affinity than adult hemoglobin (HbA).

Important one-liners for upcoming exams
☛ Which metal is present in hemoglobin? → Iron (Fe)
☛ What transports oxygen in blood? → Hemoglobin
☛ What is the Bohr Effect related to? → Oxygen release
☛ Anemia is caused by a deficiency of? → Hemoglobin
☛ What is oxyhemoglobin? → Hemoglobin + Oxygen
question_hi:
मनुष्यों में निम्न में से किसमें ऑक्सीजन के लिए उच्च बंधुता है?

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options_hi: हिमोग्लोबिन
कार्बन डाइऑक्साइड
श्वेत रक्त कोशिकाएं
मेलेनिन
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है हिमोग्लोबिन

Explanation:
हिमोग्लोबिन (Hemoglobin) एक प्रोटीन है जो लाल रक्त कोशिकाओं (RBCs) में पाया जाता है और इसका मुख्य कार्य फेफड़ों से ऑक्सीजन को शरीर के विभिन्न ऊतकों तक पहुँचाना है। हिमोग्लोबिन में आयरन (Fe²⁺) युक्त हीम (Heme) समूह होता है, जो ऑक्सीजन के साथ उच्च बंधुता (High Affinity) दर्शाता है। यह ऑक्सीजन के साथ अस्थायी रूप से बंधकर ऑक्सीहीमोग्लोबिन (Oxyhemoglobin) बनाता है। हिमोग्लोबिन की यह विशेषता शरीर में ऑक्सीजन के परिवहन को कुशल बनाती है।

Extra Facts:
हिमोग्लोबिन की ऑक्सीजन के प्रति बंधुता pH, तापमान और CO₂ सांद्रता पर निर्भर करती है। बोहर प्रभाव (Bohr Effect) के अनुसार, CO₂ की उच्च सांद्रता और कम pH (अम्लीय वातावरण) हिमोग्लोबिन की ऑक्सीजन के प्रति बंधुता को कम कर देते हैं, जिससे ऊतकों को ऑक्सीजन मुक्त हो जाती है। हिमोग्लोबिन की कमी से एनीमिया (Anemia) होता है।

question:
_______ are the vessels which carry blood away from the heart to various organs of the body.

[SSC MTS 2022]
options: Veins
Tracheas
Arteries
Plasma
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Arteries

Explanation:
Arteries are blood vessels that carry oxygen-rich blood away from the heart to various organs of the body. They have thick, elastic walls to withstand high pressure generated by the heart's pumping action. The largest artery, the Aorta, originates from the heart and branches out to supply blood throughout the body. Unlike veins, arteries lack valves because the heart's pressure ensures unidirectional blood flow.

Extra Facts:
• Veins carry deoxygenated blood back to the heart and contain valves to prevent backflow.
• Capillaries are tiny vessels connecting arteries and veins, facilitating exchange of nutrients/wastes between blood and tissues.
• The Pulmonary Artery is unique as it carries deoxygenated blood (from the heart to the lungs).

☛ Largest artery in the human body? → Aorta
☛ Vein carrying oxygenated blood to the heart? → Pulmonary vein
☛ Protein aiding blood clotting? → Fibrinogen
☛ Number of chambers in the human heart? → 4 (2 Atria, 2 Ventricles)

solution_hi:

Explanation:
धमनियाँ (Arteries) वे रक्त वाहिकाएँ हैं जो ऑक्सीजन युक्त रक्त को हृदय से शरीर के विभिन्न अंगों तक पहुँचाती हैं। ये मोटी और लचीली दीवारों वाली होती हैं, क्योंकि इन्हें हृदय के पंप करने के दौरान उच्च दबाव का सामना करना पड़ता है। इनकी मुख्य धमनी महाधमनी (Aorta) होती है, जो हृदय से निकलकर पूरे शरीर में रक्त का संचार करती है। धमनियों में वाल्व नहीं होते, क्योंकि हृदय का दबाव ही रक्त को एक दिशा में प्रवाहित करने के लिए पर्याप्त होता है।

• शिराएँ (Veins) ऑक्सीजन रहित रक्त को शरीर से वापस हृदय तक ले जाती हैं। इनमें वाल्व होते हैं जो रक्त के उल्टे प्रवाह को रोकते हैं।
• केपिलरीज (Capillaries) सूक्ष्म रक्त वाहिकाएँ होती हैं जो धमनियों और शिराओं को जोड़ती हैं तथा ऊतकों के साथ पदार्थों का आदान-प्रदान करती हैं।
• फुफ्फुसीय धमनी (Pulmonary Artery) एकमात्र ऐसी धमनी है जो ऑक्सीजन रहित रक्त ले जाती है (हृदय से फेफड़ों तक)।

question:
Who discovered blood groups?

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: Karl Landsteiner
Dmitri Mendeleev
Alexander Fleming
Isaac Newton
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Karl Landsteiner

Explanation:
Karl Landsteiner discovered blood groups (A, B, AB, O) in 1901. He found that human blood can be classified into different groups based on the presence of antigens and antibodies. This discovery was crucial for making blood transfusions safe, as using the wrong blood group could cause fatal reactions. For this work, he was awarded the Nobel Prize in 1930.

Extra Facts:
☛ The blood group system is called the ABO system, where group O is the universal donor and group AB is the universal recipient.
☛ In 1940, Landsteiner and Wiener discovered the Rh factor, which helps understand problems caused by Rh incompatibility during pregnancy.

question:
Crocodiles have a _____ chambered heart.

[SSC CGL 2019]
options: two
four
three
single
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is four

Explanation:
Crocodiles have a four-chambered heart, which distinguishes them from other reptiles. Their heart consists of two atria and two ventricles, preventing the mixing of oxygenated and deoxygenated blood and enabling efficient oxygen supply. This adaptation aids in prolonged underwater submersion. Most other reptiles (e.g., lizards) typically have a three-chambered heart with partial blood mixing.

Extra Facts:
• Crocodiles belong to the order Crocodilia and are among the oldest living reptiles.
• Their heart has a unique structure called the Foramen of Panizza, which regulates blood flow between ventricles.
• They are ectothermic (cold-blooded) but exhibit high metabolic activity compared to other reptiles.

question:
In a human body, salts are transported by:

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options:
Pulse

Oxygen

Hemoglobin

Blood
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Blood

Explanation:
In the human body, salts are transported by blood. Blood contains a fluid called plasma, which carries water, proteins, hormones, salts, and other nutrients to different parts of the body. Plasma constitutes about 55% of blood and dissolves various salts like sodium, potassium, calcium, etc., transporting them throughout the body. Oxygen is transported by hemoglobin, while salts are primarily transported through plasma, which is a component of blood.

Extra Facts:
Blood consists of three main types of cells - Red Blood Cells (RBCs), White Blood Cells (WBCs), and Platelets. RBCs transport oxygen, while WBCs are part of the immune system. Plasma contains 90% water and 10% dissolved substances (proteins, glucose, salts, etc.). The pH of blood is 7.4, which is slightly alkaline.

solution:

Explanation:
Bone marrow primarily produces three types of blood cells: Red Blood Cells (RBCs), White Blood Cells (WBCs), and Platelets. Bone marrow is of two types: Red Bone Marrow (produces blood cells) and Yellow Bone Marrow (stores fat). In adults, red marrow is mainly found in flat bones (e.g., vertebrae, ribs, pelvis). question:
What is the function of RBC in the human body?

options: To provide oxygen to the body cells
To provide digested food to the body cells
To remove nitrogenous wastes in dissolved form
To extract carbon dioxide from the body cells
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is To provide oxygen to the body cells

Explanation:
RBCs (Red Blood Cells) primarily function to transport oxygen to the body's tissues. They contain hemoglobin, a protein that binds oxygen in the lungs and delivers it to various tissues. Additionally, RBCs carry carbon dioxide from tissues back to the lungs for exhalation. This process is vital for respiration and maintaining cellular metabolism.

Extra Facts:
- The lifespan of an RBC is approximately 120 days, and they are produced in the bone marrow.
- Hemoglobin contains iron, which binds oxygen efficiently.
- RBCs lack a nucleus, allowing more space for hemoglobin and increasing oxygen-carrying capacity.

☛ Do RBCs have a nucleus? → No

question:
Identify the pigment that gives blood its colour.

[SSC CPO 2023]
options: Haemoglobin
Xanthophyll
Ferritin
Chlorophyll
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Haemoglobin

Explanation:
Haemoglobin is an iron-containing protein found in red blood cells (RBCs). It is responsible for transporting oxygen from the lungs to various tissues and carrying carbon dioxide back to the lungs. Haemoglobin contains a pigment called 'heme,' which has iron (Fe²⁺). This iron binds with oxygen, giving blood its red color. When haemoglobin is oxygenated, it appears bright red (oxyhaemoglobin), and when deoxygenated, it turns dark red (deoxyhaemoglobin).

Extra Facts:
- Haemoglobin is composed of 'heme' and 'globin' protein.
- Anaemia is a condition where haemoglobin levels drop below normal, causing fatigue and weakness.
- Carbon monoxide (CO) binds to haemoglobin 200 times more strongly than oxygen, forming 'carboxyhaemoglobin,' which disrupts oxygen transport.

question:
_______ are the vessels which carry blood away from the heart to various organs of the body.

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: Veins
Tracheas
Arteries

solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Arteries

Explanation:
Arteries are blood vessels that carry oxygenated blood from the heart to various parts of the body. They have thick, elastic walls to withstand the high pressure generated by the heart's pumping action. Unlike veins, arteries do not have valves because the heart's pressure ensures unidirectional blood flow. The aorta is the largest artery in the body, originating from the heart and distributing blood throughout the body.

Extra Facts:
Most arteries carry oxygenated blood, except the pulmonary artery, which carries deoxygenated blood from the heart to the lungs. Arterial walls consist of three layers: tunica intima, tunica media, and tunica adventitia. The study of blood vessels is called angiology. Hypertension (high blood pressure) can damage arterial walls, increasing the risk of cardiovascular diseases.

धमनियाँ (Arteries) वे रक्त वाहिकाएँ हैं जो ऑक्सीजन युक्त रक्त को हृदय से शरीर के विभिन्न अंगों तक ले जाती हैं। ये मोटी दीवारों वाली और लचीली होती हैं, क्योंकि इन्हें हृदय के पंप करने के दौरान उच्च दबाव का सामना करना पड़ता है। धमनियों में वाल्व नहीं होते हैं, क्योंकि हृदय का दबाव रक्त को एक दिशा में प्रवाहित करने के लिए पर्याप्त होता है। महाधमनी (Aorta) शरीर की सबसे बड़ी धमनी है, जो हृदय से निकलकर पूरे शरीर में रक्त का वितरण करती है।

Extra Facts:
धमनियों में ऑक्सीजन युक्त रक्त प्रवाहित होता है, लेकिन फुफ्फुसीय धमनी (Pulmonary Artery) एक अपवाद है, जो ऑक्सीजन रहित रक्त को हृदय से फेफड़ों तक ले जाती है। धमनियों की दीवारें तीन परतों से बनी होती हैं: ट्यूनिका इंटीमा, ट्यूनिका मीडिया और ट्यूनिका एडवेंटिशिया। धमनियों का अध्ययन 'एंजियोलॉजी' (Angiology) के अंतर्गत किया जाता है। उच्च रक्तचाप (Hypertension) धमनियों की दीवारों को नुकसान पहुँचा सकता है, जिससे हृदय रोगों का खतरा बढ़ जाता है।

question:
What is the pH of human blood ?

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: 6.5
5.8
10
7.4
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 7.4

Explanation:
The pH of human blood ranges between 7.35 to 7.45, which is slightly alkaline. This pH is crucial for various biochemical processes in the body. The blood pH is regulated by the buffer system, primarily the carbonic acid-bicarbonate buffer system. If the blood pH deviates from this range, it can lead to severe conditions like acidosis or alkalosis, which can be life-threatening.

Extra Facts:
pH (Potential of Hydrogen) measures the acidity or alkalinity of a substance on a scale of 0 to 14, where 7 is neutral, below 7 is acidic, and above 7 is alkaline. Different bodily fluids have varying pH levels, such as gastric juice (1.5-3.5), urine (4.6-8.0), and saliva (6.5-7.5). Maintaining blood pH is vital for the body's homeostasis.

[RRB NTPC CBT]

solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है 7.4

Explanation:
मानव रक्त का pH मान 7.35 से 7.45 के बीच होता है, जो कि हल्का क्षारीय (alkaline) होता है। यह pH शरीर के विभिन्न जैव रासायनिक प्रक्रियाओं (biochemical processes) के लिए आवश्यक होता है। रक्त का pH बफर सिस्टम (buffer system) द्वारा नियंत्रित होता है, जिसमें कार्बोनिक एसिड-बाइकार्बोनेट बफर सिस्टम (carbonic acid-bicarbonate buffer system) प्रमुख है। यदि रक्त का pH इस सीमा से बाहर हो जाता है, तो यह एसिडोसिस (acidosis) या अल्कालोसिस (alkalosis) जैसी गंभीर स्थितियों को जन्म दे सकता है, जो जीवन के लिए खतरनाक हो सकती हैं।

Extra Facts:
pH (पोटेंशियल ऑफ हाइड्रोजन) एक पदार्थ की अम्लीयता या क्षारीयता का माप है। यह 0 से 14 के पैमाने पर मापा जाता है, जहां 7 तटस्थ (neutral), 7 से कम अम्लीय (acidic), और 7 से अधिक क्षारीय (alkaline) होता है। मानव शरीर में विभिन्न तरल पदार्थों के अलग-अलग pH मान होते हैं, जैसे कि गैस्ट्रिक जूस (1.5-3.5), मूत्र (4.6-8.0), और लार (6.5-7.5)। रक्त का pH शरीर के होमियोस्टेसिस (homeostasis) को बनाए रखने के लिए अत्यंत महत्वपूर्ण है।

question:
A person with a very low count of red blood cells is medically known to have _______.

[SSC MTS 2024]
options: Anaemia
Jaundice
Goitre
Scurvy
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Anaemia

Explanation:
Anaemia is a condition characterized by a deficiency of red blood cells (RBCs) or haemoglobin in the blood. Haemoglobin is a protein that carries oxygen from the lungs to the body's tissues. Causes of anaemia include iron deficiency, lack of vitamin B12 or folic acid, blood loss, or other medical conditions. Symptoms include fatigue, weakness, shortness of breath, and pale skin. Anaemia is diagnosed through a Complete Blood Count (CBC) test.

Extra Facts:
1. Iron-deficiency anaemia is the most common nutritional disorder worldwide, especially among women and children.
2. Haemoglobin contains iron, which helps bind and release oxygen.
3. Vitamin B12 deficiency can lead to pernicious anaemia, a severe type of anaemia.
4. Sickle cell anaemia is a genetic disorder where RBCs become abnormally shaped.

☛ What disease is caused by iron deficiency? → Anaemia
☛ What happens due to vitamin B12 deficiency? → Pernicious anaemia
☛ Sickle cell anaemia is an example of what? → Genetic disorder
☛ How is anaemia diagnosed? → CBC (Complete Blood Count)

Explanation:
एनीमिया एक ऐसी स्थिति है जिसमें रक्त में लाल रक्त कोशिकाओं (RBCs) या हीमोग्लोबिन की संख्या सामान्य से कम हो जाती है। हीमोग्लोबिन एक प्रोटीन है जो फेफड़ों से ऑक्सीजन को शरीर के विभिन्न ऊतकों तक पहुँचाता है। एनीमिया के कारणों में आयरन की कमी, विटामिन B12 या फोलिक एसिड की कमी, रक्तस्राव, या अन्य चिकित्सीय स्थितियाँ शामिल हो सकती हैं। इसके लक्षणों में थकान, कमजोरी, सांस लेने में तकलीफ, और त्वचा का पीला पड़ना शामिल हैं। एनीमिया का निदान रक्त परीक्षण (CBC) द्वारा किया जाता है।

question:
People with which of the following blood groups are considered as universal recipients?

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: B+
AB+
A+
O+
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is AB+

Explanation:
People with AB+ blood group are considered as 'universal recipients' because their blood contains A, B, and Rh (D) antigens but no antibodies. This means AB+ individuals can receive blood from any blood group (A+, A-, B+, B-, AB+, AB-, O+, O-). This is possible due to the presence of antigens in their blood, which do not react with antibodies from other blood groups. Hence, in emergency situations, AB+ individuals can receive blood from any donor.

Extra Facts:
O- blood group individuals are called 'universal donors' because their blood lacks antigens, making it compatible with any blood group. Blood groups are determined by the presence or absence of antigens (A, B, and Rh) on red blood cells. Blood transfusion requires careful matching of blood groups to prevent immune reactions in the recipient's body.

☛ From whom can AB+ individuals receive blood? → All blood groups
☛ How are blood groups determined? → Based on antigens (A, B, and Rh)
☛ Which blood group has no antigens? → O-
☛ What is crucial during blood transfusion? → Blood group compatibility

question:
Which of the following statements is INCORRECT

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: Blood helps in sensory inputs
Blood carries oxygen from the lungs to the other parts of the body.
Blood protects the body from disease
Blood carries carbon dioxide from the body cells to the lungs/
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Blood helps in sensory inputs

Explanation:
The primary functions of blood include transporting oxygen, nutrients, hormones, and waste products throughout the body. It carries oxygen from the lungs to various body parts (option b is correct) and transports carbon dioxide from body cells to the lungs (option d is correct). White blood cells (WBCs) present in the blood protect the body from diseases (option c is correct). However, blood has no direct role in sensory inputs. Sensory inputs are processed by the nervous system, not by blood. Therefore, option a is incorrect.

Extra Facts:
Blood is a vital fluid connective tissue composed of plasma and blood cells. Plasma is the liquid part of blood, made up of water, proteins, salts, and other substances. Blood cells are of three types: red blood cells (RBCs), white blood cells (WBCs), and platelets. RBCs transport oxygen, WBCs provide immunity, and platelets help in blood clotting. The pH of blood ranges between 7.35 to 7.45, making it slightly alkaline. Blood also helps in maintaining body temperature and regulating pH balance.

solution_hi:

Explanation:
रक्त का मुख्य कार्य शरीर में ऑक्सीजन, पोषक तत्वों, हार्मोन्स और अपशिष्ट पदार्थों का परिवहन करना है। यह फेफड़ों से ऑक्सीजन को शरीर के विभिन्न अंगों तक पहुँचाता है (विकल्प b सही है) और कोशिकाओं से कार्बन डाइऑक्साइड को फेफड़ों तक ले जाता है (विकल्प d सही है)। रक्त में मौजूद श्वेत रक्त कोशिकाएं (WBCs) शरीर को रोगों से बचाती हैं (विकल्प c सही है)। हालांकि, रक्त का संवेदी निविष्ट (sensory inputs) से कोई सीधा संबंध नहीं है। संवेदी निविष्ट तंत्रिका तंत्र द्वारा संसाधित की जाती है, न कि रक्त द्वारा। इसलिए, विकल्प a गलत है।

question:
Non-clotting of blood occurs because of the deficiency of:

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: Vitamin D
Vitamin A
Vitamin K
Vitamin B
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Vitamin K

Explanation:
Non-clotting of blood occurs due to the deficiency of Vitamin K. Vitamin K is essential for the synthesis of clotting proteins (such as prothrombin, factor VII, IX, and X) in the liver. These proteins are activated by Vitamin K, which plays a crucial role in the blood coagulation process. A deficiency of Vitamin K impairs the production of these proteins, leading to delayed or prevented blood clotting, a condition known as hemorrhagic disorder.

Extra Facts:
Vitamin K exists in two forms: K1 (phylloquinone) and K2 (menaquinone). K1 is found in green leafy vegetables, while K2 is synthesized by gut bacteria. Newborns often suffer from Vitamin K deficiency because their gut lacks bacteria, and breast milk provides insufficient amounts. Hence, a Vitamin K injection is administered at birth to prevent bleeding disorders.

Mammals have a 4-chambered heart, consisting of 2 atria (receiving chambers) and 2 ventricles (pumping chambers). This structure supports a double circulatory system, where blood passes through the heart twice—once for oxygenation in the lungs and once to deliver oxygenated blood to the body. 2. Amphibians and most reptiles have a 3-chambered heart (2 atria, 1 ventricle), allowing partial blood mixing.

3. Crocodiles are the only reptiles with a 4-chambered heart, but they retain a unique valve (foramen of Panizza) for controlled blood mixing during diving.

question:
Which among the following are commonly known as blood thinners?

[SSC MTS 2022]
options: Anticoagulants
Antibiotics
Anticaking agent
Antibodies
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Anticoagulants

Explanation:
Anticoagulants are commonly known as blood thinners because they slow down the blood clotting process. These medications inhibit the action of clotting proteins (such as fibrinogen and thrombin) in the blood. This reduces the thickness of the blood and lowers the risk of conditions like heart attacks, strokes, or deep vein thrombosis (DVT). Warfarin and Heparin are prominent examples. These drugs prevent clot formation in blood vessels, ensuring smooth blood flow.

Extra Facts:
1. Blood thinners are of two types: Anticoagulants and Antiplatelets. Aspirin is a well-known antiplatelet that prevents platelet aggregation.

2. Anticoagulants are often prescribed to patients with conditions like Atrial Fibrillation or Artificial Heart Valves.

3. Overuse of these drugs can increase the risk of bleeding, so they should only be taken under medical supervision.

☛ Which drug is used to prevent heart attacks? → Aspirin

☛ Where is Heparin found? → Liver and Lungs
☛ What does DVT stand for? → Deep Vein Thrombosis

3. इन दवाओं के अत्यधिक उपयोग से रक्तस्राव (Bleeding) का खतरा बढ़ सकता है, इसलिए इन्हें डॉक्टर की सलाह पर ही लेना चाहिए।

question:
The liquid part of human blood , called_______, is made of water, salts and protein.

[NTPC CBT 2]
options: Platelets
RBC
Plasma
WBC
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Plasma

Explanation:
The liquid part of human blood is called plasma, which constitutes about 55% of blood volume. It is yellowish in color and primarily consists of water (90-92%), salts, proteins (7-8%) (like albumin, globulin, fibrinogen), hormones, gases, and waste products. Plasma's main functions include transporting blood cells (RBCs, WBCs, platelets) throughout the body, distributing nutrients and hormones, removing waste, and aiding in blood clotting.

Extra Facts:
• Fibrinogen in plasma plays a vital role in blood clotting.
• Plasma donation (plasmapheresis) is a medical procedure used to treat burn victims, hemophilia, and immunodeficiency disorders.
• Without plasma, blood cells cannot function properly as it acts as their transport medium.

☛ What is the primary role of platelets? → Blood clotting

question:
Which of the following is NOT found in human blood?

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: Monocyte
Leucocyte
Lymphocyte
Chondrocyte
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Chondrocyte

Explanation:
Chondrocyte is not found in human blood. Chondrocytes are specialized cells found in cartilage and are responsible for the formation and maintenance of cartilage. On the other hand, Monocytes, Leucocytes (white blood cells), and Lymphocytes are all found in human blood. Monocytes and Lymphocytes are types of Leucocytes that are part of the immune system and help fight infections.

Extra Facts:
Blood primarily consists of four components: Plasma, Red Blood Cells (RBCs), White Blood Cells (WBCs), and Platelets. WBCs are further divided into five major types: Neutrophils, Lymphocytes, Monocytes, Eosinophils, and Basophils. Chondrocytes, however, are part of connective tissue and play a crucial role in the formation of cartilage.

question:
Who performs the task of capturing oxygen in the blood?

[SSC CGL 2019]
options: Red blood cells
Chlorophyll
White blood cells
Haemoglobin
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Haemoglobin

Explanation:
Haemoglobin is a protein found in red blood cells (RBCs) that contains iron (Fe) and binds oxygen in the lungs to transport it to tissues throughout the body. Each haemoglobin molecule consists of four heme groups, each capable of binding one oxygen (O2) molecule. Thus, one haemoglobin can carry up to four oxygen molecules. This process is called oxygenation.

Extra Facts:
- Haemoglobin gives blood its red colour due to the presence of iron.
- Carbon monoxide (CO) binds to haemoglobin 200-300 times more strongly than oxygen, leading to carbon monoxide poisoning.
- Low haemoglobin levels cause anaemia, where the body does not receive enough oxygen.

solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है हीमोग्लोबिन

Explanation:
हीमोग्लोबिन (Haemoglobin) एक प्रोटीन है जो लाल रक्त कोशिकाओं (RBCs) में पाया जाता है। यह आयरन (Fe) युक्त अणु होता है जो फेफड़ों से ऑक्सीजन को बांधकर शरीर के विभिन्न ऊतकों तक पहुंचाता है। हीमोग्लोबिन में चार हीम समूह होते हैं, जिनमें से प्रत्येक एक ऑक्सीजन अणु (O2) को बांध सकता है। इस प्रकार, एक हीमोग्लोबिन अणु अधिकतम चार ऑक्सीजन अणुओं को ले जा सकता है। यह प्रक्रिया ऑक्सीजनेशन कहलाती है।

- हीमोग्लोबिन का स्तर कम होने पर एनीमिया नामक रोग हो जाता है, जिसमें शरीर को पर्याप्त ऑक्सीजन नहीं मिल पाता।
